0: Every run starts with a task. It is all the first agent knows at the start.
1: The Planner starts with a role: break the task into a short plan. It does not do the work itself.
3: The Planner's plan. Only this text is passed on to the next agent.
4: A handoff passes that text to the next agent, which sees the task and this text, nothing else.
5: The Researcher's role: collect the facts the task needs. It may use the web search tool.
7: The Researcher asks for a tool. The model only asks; the application runs the search.
8: The search results come back as text. They are data from outside, not instructions.
9: The Researcher's findings, with the gaps it noticed. They are passed on to the Writer.
11: The Writer's role: write the final answer from the material it was given.
13: The Writer's draft. It is passed on to the Fact checker.
15: The Fact checker is a free agent. Its name and instructions were written by the person who built this run.
17: The Fact checker returns the whole corrected draft, with the costs that were missing.
19: The Editor is a second free agent, with its own instructions: make the text short for a busy manager.
21: The Editor's text is the last output, so it becomes the final answer.
22: The run ends. Each agent saw only what the one before it passed on.
